questions.text: Under the RA 9266 IRR, who is a foreign architect?

options.text: Any designer employed by a foreign company
A non-Filipino architect not registered and licensed in the Philippines but duly licensed in the home country
Any Philippine registered architect working abroad
Any consultant paid in foreign currency

questions.rationale: The definition requires non-Filipino status, lack of Philippine registration and licensure, and home-country architectural licensure.

questions.text: What must a foreign architect secure before assuming architectural consultant duties in the Philippines?

options.text: A private invitation from the owner
A special or temporary permit from the Board, subject to Commission approval
A foreign firm employment contract
A local business card with an architect title

questions.rationale: RA 9266 Section 38 requires the permit before duties, functions, and responsibilities are assumed.

questions.text: How does the PRBoA temporary-permit resolution treat the permit?

options.text: It licenses the entire foreign firm for all Philippine work
It is issued to an individual foreign architect for one project and a limited period
It is permanent once issued
It replaces the Filipino counterpart requirement

questions.rationale: The PRBoA source frames the permit as individual, project-specific, and limited.

questions.text: What distinguishes special permits from temporary permits for foreign architects?

options.text: Special permits are project-specific; temporary permits are open-ended and valid for any project
Temporary permits require endorsement; special permits do not require any professional endorsement
Special permits are discretionary based on exceptional expertise; temporary permits are project-specific
Special permits are permanent; temporary permits are short-term and expire after the project concludes

rationale.a: Reverses the scope—temporary permits are project-specific; special permits allow broader consulting work.
rationale.b: Misattributes endorsement—both may require endorsement; the distinction is about expertise level and discretion.
rationale.d: Oversimplifies duration—both are limited-term; the distinction is about approval discretion and scope, not permanence.
rationale.correct: Special permits authorize consulting services requiring exceptional expertise unavailable domestically and are discretionary; temporary permits are project-specific and regularly granted.
rationale.takeaway: Special permits are selective and expertise-based (heritage conservation, complex engineering); temporary permits are routine project authorizations.

questions.text: How does the requirement for a Filipino counterpart affect fee collection by foreign architects?

options.text: Foreign architects collect fees directly from clients, bypassing local regulations and ensuring full control over their earnings
All compensation flows through the Filipino counterpart or employing firm
Fees are paid directly to the Board, which distributes them according to a predetermined schedule and ensures compliance with local laws
Foreign architects cannot receive compensation under any circumstance, as local laws prohibit direct payment to non-Filipino entities

rationale.a: Violates the counterpart requirement—direct fee collection bypasses Filipino professional oversight.
rationale.c: Attributes false intermediary role—the Board does not manage fee distribution.
rationale.d: Overstates restriction—foreign architects do receive compensation, but indirectly through Filipino firms.
rationale.correct: Foreign architects cannot collect professional fees directly; compensation flows through Filipino counterparts or employing firms for professional oversight.
rationale.takeaway: Foreign architects receive compensation only through their Filipino counterpart or employer—direct billing to clients is prohibited.

questions.text: What is the safest answer when a foreign architect is licensed abroad but not registered in the Philippines?

options.text: The architect may practice freely because licensure exists somewhere
Home-country licensure alone is not enough for Philippine practice
The architect may sign as AOR if the client agrees
The architect may bypass the Board if a Filipino firm is also hired

questions.rationale: Foreign licensure supports eligibility facts but does not remove the Philippine permit and counterpart gates.

questions.text: What documentation is required from foreign architects seeking temporary permits?

options.text: Only a valid passport, which must be valid for at least six months beyond the intended stay
Home country license, educational credentials, passport, and immigration clearance
Proof of employment by a Philippine firm, including a notarized contract and company profile
Only Board application form, which must be submitted in duplicate with a recent photograph

rationale.a: Grossly understates requirements—a passport alone proves identity, not professional qualifications.
rationale.c: Confuses cause with evidence—employment is the context, not a documentation requirement.
rationale.d: Omits substantive proof—the application form is the vehicle; credentials and documentation are the content.
rationale.correct: Foreign applicants must provide passport information, Bureau of Immigration clearance, authenticated educational transcripts, and home country professional license documentation.
rationale.takeaway: Foreign permit applications require comprehensive documentation: passport, immigration clearance, educational credentials, and home-country license—not just one document.

questions.text: What is a violation risk under the PRBoA temporary-permit source?

options.text: Refusing to use a foreign consultant
Practicing or implying legal practice without a valid temporary or special permit
Hiring a Filipino counterpart
Listing the project location in the contract

questions.rationale: The resolution identifies practice without a valid permit and misleading implications of legal practice as violation risks.

questions.text: Which statement best describes the Filipino counterpart?

options.text: A translator with construction vocabulary
The local Philippine architect, partnership, or corporation associated with the foreign participant on Philippine soil
A client-appointed marketing representative
Any local employee of the foreign firm

questions.rationale: The IRR definition ties the counterpart to local professional practice association, not clerical assistance.
questions.explanation: Ignores reciprocity check—license validity is separate from the conditional reciprocity verification. Attributes irrelevant requirement—language proficiency is not part of formal reciprocity or endorsement. Mistakes precedent for requirement—prior experience is not a reciprocity or endorsement requirement. The architect must first establish reciprocity status by proving Japan grants Filipino architects equal rights to practice; then obtain formal endorsement from Japanese authorities. Before a Japanese architect can practice in the Philippines, reciprocal rights for Filipinos in Japan must be verified and officially endorsed.

questions.text: What should an LEA answer reject in a foreign-architect fact pattern?

options.text: Checking permit timing
Automatic Philippine practice authority based only on foreign prestige or a foreign license
Checking counterpart responsibility
Applying RA 9266 Section 38

questions.rationale: The foreign-architect gate is legal authority in the Philippines, not prestige or home-country licensure alone.
